statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail remains well below the block threshold while Stress stays elevated on the scheduled Jackson Hole catalyst stack.
recommendation: Conditions are described as orderly and range-bound ahead of the 14:00Z Warsh keynote. The narrow danger window spans 13:30Z-15:30Z, covering the U.S. cash open, Chicago PMI and the keynote reaction. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NQ holds a contained overnight range under Thursday's Nvidia-led close, with the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote as the day's decisive checkpoint
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Thursday at 29,641.56, up 1.43% and effectively at the session high of 29,643.53, after Nvidia's fiscal Q2 report drove an almost 9% move in the stock and the best technology-sector day since 4 August. Overnight and into the European morning, NQ futures have given back part of that advance to about 29,605, roughly 0.31% lower, and are still trading inside the same contained 29,578.25-29,707.00 range seen an hour earlier, with genuine two-way retracement rather than one-way extension and no new session extreme. Marvell's post-earnings drop of more than 7% continues to hold Nasdaq futures behind S&P 500 and Dow futures. Cross-asset signals are calm: VIX is 14.50 and little changed, Treasury futures are essentially unchanged, the 2-year is 4.19% and the 10-year 4.66% on the latest H.15 data, and WTI has eased to about $83.03 with Brent near $88.10 as traders monitor Middle East developments without new verified escalation. The dominant scheduled risk is Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote at 14:00Z, arriving alongside the BLS preliminary payroll benchmark revision and the final Michigan sentiment reading, and 15 minutes after Chicago PMI. Survey work suggests a plurality of economists expect no explicit rate guidance, so the reaction risk is two-sided. Because no persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback continuation or session-extreme holding has been observed, the catalyst stack is scored as Stress and as conditional forecast risk rather than as current Tail. CME equity index futures settle at 21:00Z for the weekend, so the final twelve forecast hours cover a closed market. The shared Finviz context file was 139 minutes old at run time and therefore outside its freshness window; it was not used as evidence, and this assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment stayed in the EA_ON state with Tail between 10 and 14 and Stress between 45 and 54. Two hours late in Thursday's U.S. session were scored trend-up as the Nvidia-driven advance carried the index to a close at 29,641.56, near the day's high. Overnight and early European hours reverted to mixed as futures gave back part of the move inside a contained range, with the most recent hour at Tail 12 and Stress 53. One hour, 09:00Z on 27 August, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits into three phases. Through 12:00Z the base case is continued two-way trade inside the overnight range with Stress drifting up on pre-event positioning. From 13:00Z to 15:00Z the U.S. cash open, Chicago PMI at 13:45Z and the Warsh keynote at 14:00Z form the highest-risk stretch, peaking at the 14:00Z hour where the mapped policy state is WATCH; a delayed, rates-first second leg is carried as a real conditional path. From 16:00Z conditional risk decays on the assumption that price discovery is orderly and retracements return. CME equity index futures settle at 21:00Z for the weekend, so the final twelve hours cover a closed market where mean-reversion failure is structurally impossible and the residual scores represent unexpressed weekend headline accumulation ahead of the Sunday 22:00Z reopen.
